title: Integer open extensions admit a nested-open inclusion
statement: Let X be a topological space and V⊆U open subsets. For extension by zero [def-sc-abelian-open-extension-by-zero] of constant integer sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], there exists f:j_V!Z_V→j_U!Z_U such that its stalk map [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at each x∈V is an isomorphism. No compactness or quotient sheaf is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 0A38, final paragraph, and Lemma 00A5(3); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A38 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00A5

proof.text: Identify j_V!Z and j_U!Z with sheafifications of the slice extension presheaves of C=Z_X, by the constant integer open-extension comparison. On an open W, send the summand indexed by an arrow W→V to the summand indexed by W→V→U, acting identically on C(W). Naturality follows because both restriction operations precompose the arrow and restrict the same section. Thus there is a morphism of extension presheaves.

For W⊆V, both sums have one summand C(W), and the index map identifies them by the identity. At x∈V, neighborhoods contained in V are cofinal, hence the induced presheaf stalk map is an isomorphism. The sheafification units are stalk isomorphisms, naturally in the presheaf. Conjugate the sheafified map by the two comparison isomorphisms to obtain f. Its stalk map is an isomorphism at every point of V. V empty gives a vacuous condition, and V=U gives the identity index map.

lean.statement:
theorem abelianIntegerOpen_exists_inclusion
    (X : TopCat.{u}) (U V : Opens X) (hVU : V ≤ U) :
    ∃ f : (abelianOpenExtensionByZero V).obj
          ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj V))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) ⟶
      (abelianOpenExtensionByZero U).obj
          ((constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((Opens.toTopCat X).obj U))
            AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))),
      ∀ x : X, x ∈ V →
        IsIso ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} x).map f.hom)
